chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy upon him, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Sabah al-Kinani, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Among the most difficult of what servants have done is the individual's fairness towards himself, the individual's consolation with his brother, and mentioning Allah in all cases. He said: I said: May Allah rectify you, and what is the indication of mentioning Allah in all cases? He said: That one mentions Allah at the committing of an act of disobedience that one intends, at which the mentioning of Allah appears between him and between that act of disobedience, and that is the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He:
Indeed, those who are godfearing, if they are touched by an impulse from Shaytan, they remember Allah, and at once they are insightful.

key_terms.إِنصَافُ الْمَرْءِ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ: Fairness/justice of the individual towards himself

ai.seo_question: How does constant remembrance of Allah prevent sin according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing that self-accountability (muhasabah) and empathy are foundational to spiritual discipline. The Imam clarifies that constant dhikr serves as an immediate cognitive barrier against sin, transforming intention into action prevention. This concept aligns with the Shia understanding of 'tadhakkur' as a dynamic state of awareness that interrupts the ego's impulse, rather than merely ritualistic recitation.
